title: Gene mutations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: GE06a#t3 term and clue written for the game; GE06a#t2 term and clue written for the game; GE06a#t1 term and clue written for the game; GE06a#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: GE06a#N.3, GE06b#N.10, GE06a#N.6b, GE06b#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Deletion
items.clue: Loss of a base from the sequence, leaving it one base shorter.

items.label: Substitution
items.clue: One base is replaced by another, so the sequence stays the same length.

items.label: Gene mutation
items.clue: A change in the base sequence of DNA, often an uncorrected copying error.

items.label: Frameshift
items.clue: Regrouping of every downstream triplet, because reading is in threes with no gaps.

questions.stem: Part of the base sequence of a gene is GAT TCA GGC ATT before a mutation and GAT TCG GCA TT after it. Which type of gene mutation has occurred?

options.text: A substitution of the base A by G at the sixth position in the sequence
A chromosome mutation, because the total amount of DNA has changed
A deletion of one base, which has moved every later base one position along
A substitution that has shifted the reading frame of later codons

questions.explanation: The A in the second codon is missing and every base after it has moved up one place; the mutant is one base shorter. This is a deletion.

questions.stem: Why is gene mutation described as the original source of all genetic variation?

options.text: Crossing over in meiosis creates new alleles, and mutation adds to the variation they produce
Most mutations are beneficial, so each one adds a useful new variant to the species
New alleles arise only by mutation; meiosis and fertilisation just recombine alleles that already exist
Organisms generate new alleles whenever their environment demands a new trait from them

questions.explanation: Every allele of every gene began as a mutation in a germ cell of some ancestor. Meiosis and fertilisation produce new combinations but cannot produce a new allele.

questions.stem: A student finds that a hypothetical plant carries a substitution of one nucleotide in the coding region of gene P and claims that the substitution is a silent mutation. Which observation, if made, would best support the student's claim?

options.text: The mutant's protein P has the same amino acid sequence as the normal protein P
The mutant plant has the same phenotype as a plant without the substitution
The mutant plant's cells contain none of the protein encoded by gene P
The mutant's gene P contains the same amino acids as normal gene P

questions.explanation: A silent mutation changes the nucleotide sequence without changing the amino acid sequence. An unchanged amino acid sequence in protein P is the direct evidence.

questions.stem: When a new insecticide was first used on a crop, it killed nearly all individuals of a hypothetical pest insect. After several years of use, most of the pest population was resistant. Which statement best explains how resistance became common?

options.text: The insecticide caused the mutations for resistance that the insects needed to survive its use.
Insects that survived a dose built up resistance in their bodies and passed it to their offspring.
Every insect in the population gradually became more resistant until the whole population was.
Insects that already had resistance alleles from a random mutation survived and reproduced more.
